title: Keeping pipe connections fixed during filter replacement
original: The assembly contains a housing, two interfaces, a sealing ring, a cartridge frame and two filter layers. The cartridge frame can move sideways and contains both layers. The interfaces are attached to the housing. The sealing ring is attached to the housing opening. Replacing the cartridge does not detach the housing. The conventional replacement sequence first removes the housing from the pipe. The model tracks component positions and layer order. No performance measurements are available, and flow is stopped during replacement.
revised: The candidate changes the replacement operation from disconnecting the housing to withdrawing the filter cartridge (Fig. 1). This leaves the pipe connections intact while exposing the replaceable layers. To separate these roles, both layers must leave with the frame in their original order, while the seal remains on the housing opening. Replacement takes place with flow stopped.
evidence: The supplied description reports a component-position model check, but its source model and logs were not available. The check has not been independently reproduced here. No filtration, leakage, manufacturing or replacement-time tests are available. This constructed example illustrates a design account, not validated mechanical or performance results.
caption: Figure 1. Replacement changes which assembly moves. Arrows denote component motion with flow stopped. The conventional housing is detached (a); the candidate housing, interfaces and opening seal stay fixed (b). Dashed frame and numbered layer outlines show the seated position of the same cartridge drawn in solid colour after withdrawal. Layers 1 and 2 retain their inlet-to-outlet order. The cutaway is a structural DEMO, not to scale; it does not represent pressurized replacement.
